title: Symmetry extension by condensation defects II: general dimensions and higher-groups
authors: Matteo Bertolini, Lorenzo Di Pietro, Stefano C. Lanza, Antonio Santaniello
abstract: We discuss a class of symmetry structures in general spacetime dimension that arise when gauging symmetries in theories with a cubic 't Hooft anomaly. The anomaly mixes two Abelian discrete symmetries $A$ and $B$ with a characteristic class for an additional symmetry $C$, and we gauge $A\times B$. The novelty of this construction is that the resulting symmetry structure involves certain condensation defects of the dual symmetry $\widehat{A}\times\widehat{B}$. Specifically, these defects generate an invertible symmetry that extends $C$, either as an ordinary group extension or as a higher-group, depending on the characteristic class. We describe the corresponding charged operators and states, and illustrate the mechanism in several examples.
summary: This work develops a general framework for determining how symmetry structures are modified when gauging symmetries in QFTs characterized by a cubic mixed 't Hooft anomaly. It shows that the resulting theory features an extended symmetry, which can be classified as either a simple group extension or a more complex higher-group structure. This is achieved by analyzing the behavior of condensation defects associated with dual symmetries.
main_problem: The paper investigates novel symmetry structures that emerge in Quantum Field Theories (QFTs) when gauging symmetries associated with a cubic mixed 't Hooft anomaly.
main_result: The resulting symmetry structure is an extension of the original symmetry $C(r)$ by a $\mathbb{Z}_{D(n+r-1)}$ group, which can manifest as either a standard group extension or a higher-group structure depending on the specific parameters.
method: The analysis uses anomaly inflow formulas and examines how gauging symmetries affects the topological defects and fusion rules of the resulting dual theory.
model_or_system: The study is general, starting with a $d$-dimensional QFT possessing three interacting Abelian discrete symmetries ($A(p)$, $B(q)$, and $C(r)$) characterized by a cubic mixed anomaly. Examples include QED3 and $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric QED3.
key_observables: The nature of the symmetry extension (standard vs. higher-group), the resulting discrete group structure ($\mathbb{Z}_{D(n+r-1)}$), and the fusion rules of topological operators.
important_parameters: The dimensions $d$, the charges/indices $(p, q, r)$, and the anomaly coefficients defining the cubic term are crucial parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis fundamentally relies on the existence and structure of a cubic mixed 't Hooft anomaly in the theory under consideration.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the general framework using the anomaly inflow formula, analyzing the consequences of gauging $A 	imes B$, deriving constraints on background fields from partition function invariance, and finally classifying the resulting symmetry extension based on the defect structure.
why_interesting: While highly theoretical, the concept of emergent higher-group symmetries and topological defects is relevant to understanding complex many-body ground states or effective theories derived from condensed matter systems with strong topological order.
